name: CoMTA
summary: 188 math tutoring conversations from Khan Academy's Khanmigo, anonymized and reworded, each ending on a student's answer with whether the tutor should accept it: does an AI tutor get the math right while it tutors?

license.note: Khan Academy's Evaluation Dataset License: internal, non-commercial evaluation of models only. No redistribution, publication, training or production use, and anything made from it stays under the same terms.
license.terms: internal, non-commercial evaluation of models only; no redistribution, publication, training or production use

cite: Miller, P., & DiCerbo, K. (2024). LLM Based Math Tutoring: Challenges and Dataset. Khan Academy. https://github.com/Khan/tutoring-accuracy-dataset

fits.how: Each conversation could be a test case that ends on the student's answer, with whether to accept it as the rubric, the way GSM8K's right and wrong answers are, in a real tutoring conversation.

connect.note: No connector is written yet. One would fetch it into each person's own folder for their own evaluation, which its license allows, and ask them to accept its terms first.
